speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your post-operative review. You mentioned occasional shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings after your tympanoplasty; can you describe exactly where the pain is located and what triggers it?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: The pain radiates from your ear to your jaw and is triggered by eating, while earrings cause direct discomfort; have you noticed any swelling, redness, or a lump at your surgical site, and does chewing make the pain significantly worse?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Recurrent Glossopharyngeal Neuralgia (GPN) with secondary auricular neuropathic pain following tympanoplasty.

The characteristic shooting pain triggered by eating (jaw movement) and the history of chronic ear infections suggest irritation of the glossopharyngeal nerve, possibly exacerbated by the recent surgery. The discomfort with earrings is likely due to altered sensation or scarring in the external auditory canal rather than a new infection. I will proceed with this diagnosis without further questioning, as the clinical picture is sufficient.
